questions.question: Which data structure operates strictly on a First-In, First-Out (FIFO) principle?
options: Queue
Stack
Binary Search Tree
Hash Map
questions.explanation: A Queue processes elements strictly in the order they were inserted (FIFO).
questions.subject: Data Structures & Algorithms

questions.question: How do React Server Components (RSC) fundamentally differ from standard Client Components?
options: RSCs execute exclusively on the server, producing lightweight streamed HTML without shipping component JavaScript to the client bundle
RSCs execute inside a browser Service Worker to cache offline network assets
RSCs are strictly limited to rendering static images and cannot query databases
RSCs re-render on every client mousemove event
questions.correct_answer: RSCs execute exclusively on the server, producing lightweight streamed HTML without shipping component JavaScript to the client bundle
questions.explanation: RSCs keep sensitive data, direct database connections, and heavy dependencies on the server, streaming minimal zero-bundle HTML to client browsers.
questions.subject: Full-Stack Web Development

questions.question: In PostgreSQL, what is the primary architectural security benefit of Row-Level Security (RLS)?
options: RLS security policies are enforced at the database engine level, preventing cross-tenant data leakage even if application queries omit tenant filters
RLS automatically compresses table indexes on disk
RLS eliminates the requirement for primary keys and foreign keys
RLS converts relational SQL tables into NoSQL document collections
questions.correct_answer: RLS security policies are enforced at the database engine level, preventing cross-tenant data leakage even if application queries omit tenant filters
questions.explanation: RLS policies are enforced directly by the database engine for every query, ensuring strict tenant isolation by default.
questions.subject: Database Systems

questions.question: In HTTP/1.1 semantics, which of the following request methods are guaranteed to be idempotent?
options: GET, HEAD, PUT, and DELETE
POST only
POST and PATCH only
None of the standard HTTP methods are idempotent
questions.explanation: Making multiple identical GET, HEAD, PUT, or DELETE requests produces the exact same server state as a single request.
questions.subject: Full-Stack Web Development

questions.question: Under ANSI SQL standards, which transaction isolation level provides complete immunity against Dirty Reads, Non-Repeatable Reads, and Phantom Reads?
options: SERIALIZABLE
REPEATABLE READ
READ COMMITTED
READ UNCOMMITTED
questions.explanation: SERIALIZABLE execution simulates sequential transaction execution, providing complete isolation against Dirty, Non-Repeatable, and Phantom reads.
questions.subject: Database Systems

questions.question: When verifying a JSON Web Token (JWT) signed with an asymmetric algorithm like RS256, which key must the verifying backend service use?
options: The Identity Provider's Public Key
The Identity Provider's Private Key
A symmetric shared secret password
The client browser's TLS session cookie
questions.explanation: Asymmetric signing uses the Private Key to create signatures (held by the auth issuer) and the Public Key to mathematically verify signatures.
questions.subject: Cybersecurity & Cloud Systems

questions.question: In Node.js and modern browser runtimes, what is the execution priority between Microtasks and Macrotasks?
options: All Microtasks in the microtask queue are drained before the event loop advances to the next Macrotask
Macrotasks always execute before any queued Microtasks
Microtasks and Macrotasks run concurrently across multiple OS threads
Microtasks execute only when the browser window loses focus
questions.correct_answer: All Microtasks in the microtask queue are drained before the event loop advances to the next Macrotask
questions.explanation: The event loop drains the entire microtask queue (Promise callbacks, process.nextTick, queueMicrotask) immediately after the current call stack clears and before processing the next macrotask.
questions.subject: Computer Science

questions.question: Why do Docker containers start in milliseconds with minimal memory overhead compared to traditional Type-2 Hypervisor Virtual Machines?
options: Containers share the host operating system kernel and isolate user space using cgroups/namespaces, whereas VMs emulate virtual hardware and boot a full guest OS
Containers bypass the CPU and execute exclusively on GPU Tensor cores
Containers compile application source code directly to hardware microcode
Containers disable all filesystem write permissions
questions.correct_answer: Containers share the host operating system kernel and isolate user space using cgroups/namespaces, whereas VMs emulate virtual hardware and boot a full guest OS
questions.explanation: Containers are lightweight processes sharing the host Linux kernel through namespaces and cgroups, avoiding the guest OS initialization overhead of virtual machines.
questions.subject: DevOps & Cloud Infrastructure

questions.question: In the Cache-Aside (Lazy Loading) caching pattern, how does the application handle a cache miss?
options: The application queries the primary database, populates the retrieved data into the cache, and returns it to the client
The application returns a 404 Not Found error response immediately
The cache engine automatically triggers a database query via native database extensions
The application blocks all incoming HTTP requests until a cache warmup script finishes
questions.correct_answer: The application queries the primary database, populates the retrieved data into the cache, and returns it to the client
questions.explanation: Under Cache-Aside, the application first inspects the cache; upon a miss, it queries the database, writes the result into the cache with a TTL, and serves the caller.
questions.subject: Enterprise Architecture

questions.question: Why is a B-Tree index preferred over a Hash index for database columns frequently queried with range operators (e.g., BETWEEN, <, >)?
options: B-Tree keeps index keys in sorted order with doubly linked leaf nodes for rapid range scans, whereas Hash index only supports O(1) equality lookups
Hash indexes cannot store integers or timestamps
B-Tree indexes do not consume disk storage
Hash indexes require distributed 2-phase commit protocols for every query
questions.correct_answer: B-Tree keeps index keys in sorted order with doubly linked leaf nodes for rapid range scans, whereas Hash index only supports O(1) equality lookups
questions.explanation: B-Tree leaf nodes form a sorted doubly linked list allowing efficient range scans, whereas hash functions distribute keys randomly across buckets, making range queries impossible.
questions.subject: Database Systems
